affordance_in_statement: it is guaranteed by the physical design that destructive interference can only ever occur between two components of opposite polarities. Two components with the same polarity will never interfere.
removal_suggestion: The guarantee can only be removed by allowing interference graphs with odd cycles; merely hiding the polarity wording does not remove the underlying bipartite structure. If the task must remain bipartite, this is an intrinsic structural affordance and cannot be eliminated by rewording.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the interference graph as bipartite and reduces finding an exact-size independent set to maximum independent set via bipartite matching and Konig's theorem.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: destructive interference can only ever occur between two components of opposite polarities; same-polarity components never interfere

common_affordance: The interference graph is guaranteed to be bipartite, enabling a polynomial maximum-independent-set solution through maximum matching.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The submitted BFS implementation is incomplete or malformed in the shown excerpt, ending at a dangling "q", which causes a runtime failure.

Its coloring-based construction does not correctly compute a maximum independent set in a general bipartite graph, apparently relying on a color-class shortcut rather than the matching-based construction required for arbitrary component sizes.
It depends on scipy's sparse maximum-bipartite-matching implementation, which is unavailable in the judging environment and causes a runtime error.

recommended_edit: Remove the opposite-polarity guarantee and permit arbitrary interference graphs, including odd cycles; this directly defeats the bipartite-coloring and Konig/matching shortcut.
regression_risk: This edit changes the input class and turns the problem into general maximum independent set, so it may make the intended constraints computationally infeasible rather than merely harder.
